pages.title: Menu
pages.content:
The menu

Six baskets, folded behind the glass and steamed for seven minutes. Eat in and takeaway cost the same: pork soup dumplings €9.50, crab and pork €12.50, mushroom and greens €9.00, chicken and ginger €9.50, spicy wontons in chilli oil €8.50 and garlic greens €5.50.

pages.title: Branches
pages.content:
Three branches

Harbour Street, Linden Market and Station Arcade, all in Port Aldren. Each branch folds its own dumplings and keeps its own hours.

pages.title: Harbour Street
pages.content:
Harbour Street

12 Harbour Street, Port Aldren. The glass kitchen and flagship since 2014, with 38 seats. Open Tuesday to Sunday 11:00–21:00, closed Monday.

pages.title: Linden Market
pages.content:
Linden Market

Stall 21, Linden Covered Market, open since 2018, with 14 counter seats. Open Tuesday to Saturday 10:00–17:00.

pages.title: Station Arcade
pages.content:
Station Arcade

Unit 4, Station Arcade, open since 2022: a takeaway window and 6 stools, with the breakfast basket from 07:30. Monday to Friday 07:30–20:00, Saturday and Sunday 10:00–18:00.

pages.title: Frozen packs
pages.content:
Frozen packs

Pork, 24 for €19. Mushroom and greens, 24 for €18. Crab and pork, 18 for €22. Mixed box, 30 (10 pork, 10 mushroom, 10 chicken) for €26. Keep at −18 °C for up to three months and steam from frozen for twelve minutes. Restocked every Friday at all three branches.

pages.title: Order ahead
pages.content:
Order ahead

Send your order by 11:00 for lunch pickup 12:00–14:00, or by 16:00 for dinner pickup 17:30–20:00. For 100 or more dumplings, give 48 hours' notice. Pay when you collect, at the window you named.

pages.title: The fold

The fold

Kawa Dumpling House was founded in 2014 by Lena Kowal and Samuel Adeyemi, with one glass-walled kitchen on Harbour Street in Port Aldren.

categories.name: Kitchen notes
categories.description: The fold, the broth and the morning prep.

posts.title: How the broth gets inside
posts.excerpt: The set broth jelly is cut into cubes before it goes into the pork filling.
posts.content:
A soup dumpling is a small trick of temperature. Samuel Adeyemi simmers the broth at Harbour Street and sets it in trays at 06:30 each morning, until it holds its shape like a firm jelly.

Once set, the jelly is cut into small cubes and folded into the pork filling, fifteen grams to each dumpling. In the steamer, for seven minutes, the cubes melt back into broth inside the wrapper.

That is why the fold matters. Eighteen pleats close the wrapper tightly enough to keep the broth where it belongs until the first bite.

posts.title: A table for six at Harbour Street
posts.excerpt: Six friends share baskets at a wooden table on Harbour Street, hands reaching across the steamers.
posts.content:
The long table at the back of the Harbour Street kitchen seats six, close enough to the glass to watch the bench. Tomasz Nowak sets it with a pot of jasmine tea and a dish of black vinegar and ginger, both on the house.

A table of six usually orders three baskets of pork, one of mushroom and greens, and a round of garlic greens, then passes them around. The baskets arrive one at a time, straight from the steamer.

posts.title: Morning: the first two thousand wrappers
posts.excerpt: Wrappers are rolled to six grams on the bench before the doors open.
posts.content:
At 08:00 the doughs have rested and the rolling begins. Each wrapper is rolled by hand to six grams, thin at the edge and thicker in the middle so it can carry the filling and the broth.

By 10:30 the first folds are pleated behind the glass, and by 11:00, when the doors open, there are two thousand wrappers on the bench waiting for the day.
